relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with HA20; the paper states: "It revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20)".
method_note: Case report of one girl with HA20; one in-scope relative with individual-level facts (father: 'her father had recurrent fever and tonsillitis at preschool age') and one relative described in relation to her without individual-level detail (younger sister, NGS recommended). Her mother is never described individually (only inside 'her parents', whose testing was refused), so no 'parent of patient' row was made, to avoid duplicating the father. A previously published patient cited as reference [8] ('only 2 patients, including our case, have been diagnosed with HA20 in Korea [8]') got no row: the paper gives no individual-level description of that person. The 89-patient review [4] and the 26-study review [5] are cited at group level only. Table 1 has time points (not patients) as columns, so no stacked-cell problem arose; table cells were transcribed from the Markdown and checked against the table. Judgements: the anal ulcer was mapped to checklist item 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' (perianal/anal ulcer); checklist item 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' was left 'not reported' because the paper excludes only uveitis (narrower than the composite), while the narrower fact 'no uveitis' is recorded in phenotypic_features; similarly the father's 'did not have ... arthritis' does not exclude the composite 'arthritis or arthralgia'. Routine negative antibodies in Table 1 are recorded as excluded abnormalities (e.g. 'positive ANCA'). The c.547C>T variant is described for the patient only; zygosity and inheritance are 'not reported' because the parents refused testing. 'known to cause HA20' was recorded as the authors' pathogenicity statement for this exact variant. publications.cohort_size_as_stated is null: the authors state no total number of study patients. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = false (no statement that these patients were reported earlier). No contradictions found in the paper.
